summary:
Farming has always been a conversation with the weather, but climate change is making that conversation harder to follow. AgriShield AI helps farmers keep up. Built on NASA Earth observation and climate data, it turns satellite imagery and environmental signals into clear, practical decisions.

The platform brings together five capabilities. Our Satellite Observations Layer draws on NASA GIBS to show vegetation health through MODIS NDVI, SMAP soil moisture, true-color imagery, and NDWI water indicators. Our Yield Forecasting and Extreme Weather Risk Matrix studies Growing Degree Days, Vapor Pressure Deficit, and climate time series to flag heatwaves, flash droughts, and frost before they strike. The Smart Irrigation Calculator estimates reference evapotranspiration and crop water needs, so every drop counts. Our Alerting and Input Timing Engine highlights the best weather windows for spraying and fertilizing. Finally, the Climate Change Scenario Simulator lets users explore how shifting temperature and rainfall could affect yields and drought risk over the next ten years.

AgriShield AI answers the Field Shift challenge by making NASA data useful on the ground. By combining monitoring, forecasting, and decision support in one place, it helps farmers use resources more wisely, plan ahead with confidence, and build more resilient farms.
details:
What is AgriShield and how does it work?

AgriShield AI is a smart agricultural decision-support platform that uses NASA satellite observations and climate data to help farmers monitor crop conditions, anticipate environmental risks, and make better farming decisions.

It integrates NASA GIBS satellite imagery to display vegetation health (NDVI), soil moisture, true-color imagery, and water-related indicators. Its predictive engine analyzes Growing Degree Days (GDD), Vapor Pressure Deficit (VPD), and climate trends to identify potential heatwaves, droughts, and frost risks. It also calculates crop water requirements using evapotranspiration (ET₀), provides irrigation insights, identifies suitable weather windows for spraying and fertilizing, and offers a simulator to explore the potential effects of future climate changes on crop yields and drought risk.

Benefits:

  • Helps farmers monitor vegetation and environmental conditions.
  • Supports more informed irrigation and water-management decisions.
  • Provides early warnings of potentially damaging weather conditions.
  • Helps identify safer periods for agricultural activities.
  • Allows farmers to explore possible climate-change impacts before making decisions.

What is its intended impact?

Our goal is to make agriculture more climate-resilient by turning complex Earth observation data into understandable, actionable information. We aim to reduce uncertainty in farm planning, encourage efficient resource use, and help farmers prepare for environmental challenges.

What tools and technologies did we use?

  • Data sources: NASA GIBS, MODIS, SMAP, and NASA climate data.
  • Programming: TypeScript and JavaScript.
  • Frontend: React and a web-based application framework.
  • Libraries and modules: Custom satellite-data integration, agricultural calculation engines, and interactive simulation components.

How is the project creative?

AgriShield AI combines satellite monitoring, agricultural calculations, predictive risk analysis, automated advisories, and future climate simulations in one platform. Rather than simply displaying environmental data, it transforms observations into practical decision-support features.

What factors did our team consider?

We considered climate variability, water scarcity, extreme weather, crop growth conditions, irrigation requirements, and the timing of farming activities. We also considered the importance of making complex scientific data understandable and useful for farmers. Our approach prioritizes practical insights while recognizing that model predictions are estimates, not guarantees.
